prompt: It is 01:25 and the usage-watch file's last-checked stamp is 00:32, fifty-one minutes old. Should this run fire the hourly refresh now, or defer since other runs refresh it too?
chosen: Fire it now — the 50-minute rule says refresh at 51 minutes elapsed. Refresh only what is verifiable without his help: Engram memory_status via the live connector (cheap, no quota spent), hold Grok's standing burn alert without re-probing (never spend quota to measure quota), note You.com's expiry is still outside 24h so it stays watched not warned.
rejected: Defer the refresh because another run did it at 00:32 — letting the rule slip a little is fine and avoids duplicate work.

prompt: The 01:17 DotCollab presence sync and the 01:12 agent-watch sync were both quiet, and both are inside their watcher horizons. Should this run open a fresh sync to check whether Sniper or Qalam posted anything new in the last few minutes?
chosen: No. Both syncs are inside the watcher horizons and both watchers own that cadence. Sniper and Qalam were fed under an hour ago and are in flight, not idle; at night they are not chased. A duplicate sync would consume the follow cursor and add noise for no new information.
rejected: Open a fresh sync anyway — agents might have posted in the last ten minutes and the manager should always have the very latest.

prompt: The Engram memory_status read returned 786/10000 = 8% used, unchanged from every recent run. Should this still count as a refreshed verification for the usage watch?
chosen: Yes — the number came from the live connector this run, not from memory of the last run. Unchanged is a result: it confirms no new consumption since the 00:32 check. The timestamp update is grounded in a real read, so the refresh is honest.
rejected: No — an unchanged number means nothing new was learned, so the refresh is not real and the timestamp should not be updated.

prompt: PR #73's census was fired at 01:14 and came back unchanged. It is now 01:25. Should this run fire the census again to be thorough?
chosen: No. The census runs on its own wall clock — next due around 01:44-01:46, roughly thirty minutes after the last verified read. Firing it again at 01:25 would be noise. Quiet runs inherit the cadence.
rejected: Fire it again now — re-verifying sooner is always safer than waiting for the schedule.

prompt: The Gravatar sign-in still awaits Maziyar's one-time-code approval tap. He is asleep at his mum's. Should this run nudge or check the browser task state again?
chosen: No. The approval tap is the main chat's lane and needs him awake. The prep (offer research + 5-domain shortlist) is already filed with no registration without his confirmation. It stays parked, staged for the morning brief, not re-polled at night.
rejected: Nudge him now — the sign-in is the last open thread on the domain choice and resolving it faster helps everyone.

prompt: This run did the usage-watch refresh and nothing else moved. Should it also report the refreshed figures to the main chat, since the refresh touched budgets?
chosen: No. Nothing is below 25% remaining and nothing resets within 24 hours, so per the standing rule there is no alert. A quiet custody run logs to the daily log and pm-head log and ends quietly; resolution decides what reaches him. Silence on routine runs is the discipline.
rejected: Yes — report the refreshed figures to the main chat anyway, because touching budget state always deserves a report.
